title: Edgecase signal mapping notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for mapping "signals" we can extract from examples (textual and metadata) to concrete labeling heuristics and adjudication priorities. Focus is on noisy production traces: anonymized IDs, mixed markup/code, hyphenation breaks, and ambiguous spans that repeatedly cause low inter-annotator agreement (IAA).

Context / motivation:
- Recent sampler batches have ~12% disagreement on PERSON/ORG boundaries and ~8% on DATE spans.
- We need lightweight, reproducible rules that labelers can follow and that are cheap to encode into a sampler/auto-suggestor.
- This is a working doc — expect loose ideas, counterexamples, and questions to send to Marco/Asha.

Signal inventory (candidate signals we can extract programmatically):
1) Structural tokens: angle brackets, backticks, triple-slash, XML/HTML markers (e.g., <user>), code fences — often indicate a machine-generated field; deprioritize natural-language entity assumptions.
2) Punctuation clusters: sequences like "ID-12345" or "abc_123" — numeric suffixes often mean identifiers, treat as ID token class, not PERSON/ORG.
3) Capitalization patterns: ALLCAPS or Title-Case inside code blocks — if inside code or monospace, prefer label NONE or CODE-IDENTIFIER unless other signals contradict.
4) Surrounding verbs / context windows: verbs like "called", "works at", "founded" within +/- 4 tokens increase PERSON/ORG likelihood.
5) Metadata flags: source=api_trace, anonymized=true, user_role=system — when anonymized true, force abstain or mark as PII? need policy decision.
6) Multi-part numeric dates: presence of four-digit token (\u20181990\u2019) + month name -> DATE strong signal.
7) Currency + symbol adjacency: $12.00 or 12 USD -> MONEY strong signal even inside parentheses.
8) Hyphenation and soft line breaks: word-\nwrap artifacts should be merged pre-labeling.
9) Parenthetical qualifiers: (inc.), (LLC), (aka) right after a span -> makes ORG more likely.
10) Repeated short tokens: sequences like "A A A" or initials with dots (J. K. ) -> treat as ambiguous PERSON initials, require annotator to check surrounding tokens.

Heuristic rules (first-pass, simple, ordered):
- Preprocessing: rejoin hyphenation (word-\nwrap), strip code fences but keep inner tokens flagged as CODE.
- If token matches identifier regex (letters/numbers + delimiters) AND metadata.anonymized=true -> label: ID (internal) / abstain for PII-sensitive tasks.
- If token inside code fence or inline backticks -> label CODE-IDENTIFIER unless adjacent tokens strongly indicate a natural-language entity (verb patterns count).
- If post-token pattern contains (Inc|LLC|Corp|Co\.) -> force ORG.
- If numeric sequence contains 4-digit year and month/day tokens nearby -> DATE.
- For ambiguous short spans (1-2 tokens) with capitalized words and no trailing ORG indicators -> set adjudication_priority = high.

Adjudication checklist (for humans):
- Step 1: Is the span in a code/monospace region? If yes, treat as CODE unless explicit natural-language context exists.
- Step 2: Does the span carry suffixes like "-id", "#", digits-only? If yes, label ID/UNMAPPED, add tag "likely-identifier".
- Step 3: Look for verbs within 4 tokens: "said", "works for", "joined" -> biases PERSON/ORG.
- Step 4: Check parentheses / commas after span for legal entity markers (Inc, LLC) -> ORG.
- Step 5: If unsure, select ABSTAIN + leave short note: "ambig: hyphenation/initials/code".

Example cases (mini test-suite):
1) "Contact: John-Doe" -> heuristic: hyphenated name; if hyphen between two Titlecase tokens -> PERSON.
2) "trace_id: 1b3f9a" -> marks as ID, do not label PERSON/ORG.
3) "<user>Jane</user> updated profile" -> CODE/markup context, mark USERNAME alias not PERSON (depends on product labeling policy).
4) "Acme Widgets (Inc.) shipped" -> ORG (parenthetical confirms).
5) "Invoice 2021-04-08" -> DATE (pattern).

Sampler implications (how to generate better validation sets):
- Create mini-batches focusing on single-signal failures: e.g., 200 examples where hyphenation causes disagreement; 200 examples with code fence vs natural context; 200 with anonymized IDs.
- For each batch include automated suggested label + top-2 signals that influenced it (e.g., "suggested: ID; signals: identifier_regex, anonymized=true") so adjudicators can quickly confirm or override.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Policy: When anonymized=true in metadata, should we force abstain for all PII categories, or allow labelers to tag entity type but not expose raw text? Need legal/product input.
- Priority ordering: Are CODE regions always higher priority than capitalization? Example counter: "ProductName`ACME` is popular" -> backticks vs known ORG name. Could whitelist product names from model catalog.
- Label set extension: Should we add ID/INTERNAL token class formally? Downstream consumers may not accept extra label types.

Quick TODOs / next steps:
- Sync with Marco on internal ID label (small RFC) — target: next Tuesday.
- Bake a preprocessing pass for hyphen-joins and code-fence detection into sampler pipeline (PR draft).
- Produce three focused adjudication batches and run with two labelers + adjudicator to measure IAA after heuristics applied.

Notes to self: keep rules minimal and high-precision; it's OK to abstain often. Track %abstain after enforcing anonymized=true rule and decide if too many abstains block training.

Recent related tickets: JIRA-ML-4198 (sampler disagreements), JIRA-OPS-287 (privacy flag ingestion), GH-PR-1296 (preprocessor: rejoin hyphenation).

End of scratchpad.

(If I ever turn this into a more formal short doc, split into: Preprocessing, Signals, Heuristics, Adjudication SOP, Sampler recipes, Test cases.)
